text: A political earthquake has hit the United States midterm elections, completely reshaping the country's political map. In a historic comeback, the Democratic Party has seized control of both houses of Congress. In the House of Representatives, Democrats have surged past the magic number of 218 required for a majority, capturing over 224 seats. With this victory, Hakeem Jeffries is set to become the first black speaker of the House in American history. But the real suspense unfolded in the Senate races. Democrats pulled off stunning upsets in traditional Republican strongholds like Texas and Kansas, securing a clear majority with 52 seats in the Senate. Adding to the historic night, Democrat Abdul-El-Sayed won in Michigan, becoming the first Muslim Senator in U.S. history. Looking at the gubernatorial races, history was made across the board. In Texas, Gina Hinojosa defeated Greg Abbott to become the state's first Latina governor. While in Georgia, Keisha Lance Bottoms became the first black woman governor in U.S. history. On the flip side, Republicans held their ground in Florida, electing Byron Donalds as their new governor. These sweeping results are being viewed as a massive public mandate against President Trump's policies. Navigating the final two years of his presidential term is now going to be a monumental challenge for Trump. What do you think will be the global impact of this political shift? Let us know in the comments and follow for more updates. Important note. These results are based on preliminary media reports coming in on November 4. Vote counting and verification are still ongoing across various states, so these figures may change until the final official results are certified.
